facts.topic: TLN COO Brad Berryman's Nov 17 sale (~$19.8M)
facts.answer: The SEC Form 4 for the Nov 17 TLN sales says one or more transactions were made under a Rule 10b5-1(c) trading plan: a pre-scheduled sale, not a signal. Separately, across 129 officer open-market sales in our names (2024-2026) the stock did about the same as our basket over the next 20 days (-0.16%, t -0.1). Give it no weight.

facts.topic: PJM 2029/30 capacity auction delay
facts.answer: No FERC ruling on the new delay request was found as of Nov 25. The 2029/30 base residual auction is scheduled to close Dec 15, under the price collar (floor and cap) FERC extended to the 2028/29 and 2029/30 auctions. A Nov 3 2026 complaint (EL27-11) explicitly does not seek to disrupt the 2029/30 auction. Until a ruling appears, assume the Dec 15 auction goes ahead; it is on the calendar.

facts.topic: Discovery engine survivors checked on 2008-2026 vs the S&P
facts.answer: 3 down days: lost 2008-18, paid 2019-26 (practice book only). New 52-week high: inconsistent (5 days from the same close: miners -1.76%/-1.21% vs S&P; 10 days from the next close: -0.48%/+1.35%): do not use it either way. New 52-week low: flips between eras, no edge. Offering dilution: already a live exit rule.

facts.topic: Insider sales in general
facts.answer: Officer open-market sales in our names carry no predictive weight (129 cases, -0.16% vs basket over 20 days). Insider BUYS are rare here (11 in 2 years in our 14 names).

facts.topic: News and filings that do NOT predict our stocks
facts.answer: Checked on 2008-2026: a cheered company filing (+3% day) is not a reliable sell signal (-5.4% vs S&P 2008-18 but +0.4% 2019-26); protest/opposition news, analyst upgrades, downgrades and new coverage have no lasting effect. Do not trade or size off them. What DOES carry: a +8% earnings reaction day keeps drifting up for ~20 sessions (live rule 'earnings_pop').

facts.topic: Earnings-pop drift (live rule 'earnings_pop'): what to expect
facts.answer: Checked on 620 earnings pops in 137 big US stocks: the drift after a +8% earnings day is real but small, about +1% vs the S&P over 20 days and beating it only ~51-52% of the time. Treat each trade as a slight edge, not a sure thing; never size it up on conviction alone.

facts.topic: The recurring pattern: buying weakness in our names
facts.answer: Across nearly every 'buy after weakness' signal (3 down days, stock-level panic days, sector selloffs, volume spikes, 52-week lows), our stocks LOST vs the S&P in 2008-2018 and GAINED in 2019-2026. The live rules that buy crashes (panic, sharp drop, comeback) passed in both eras; looser versions only work in the AI era. If the market regime turns like 2008-2018, the loose versions would hurt: that is why they stay in the practice book.

facts.topic: Seasons for our basket (vs the S&P, 2008-2026)
facts.answer: January-February has been the best stretch: our 10 beat the S&P by +3.7% (2008-18, 6 of 11 years) and +5.7% (2019-26, 7 of 8); related stocks +0.7% / +3.7%. November has been mildly weak in both eras for both groups (our 10 -1.2% / -3.1%). March was weak for our 10 (-7.9% / -3.2%) but not for related stocks, so treat that as noise. Only ~19 years per month: use as a tilt in the daily stance, not a trade.

facts.topic: Fear gauges beyond the VIX
facts.answer: SKEW (crash pricing) and VIX9D-over-VIX (short-term panic) did not predict our basket vs the S&P in either era. A VVIX spike (top 5% of the past year) flipped: -3.0% in 2008-18, +3.3% in 2019-26 over 10 days; it is in the practice book, no money.

facts.topic: Reactor restart news: sell-the-news
facts.answer: After restart headlines (Japan, Palisades, Three Mile Island and others), the named stock lagged the S&P over the next 5 days in every sample: -2.8% (2019-22, n 30, t -2.4), -2.2% (2023-26, n 134, t -3.7), -2.1% (2008-18, only 6 cases). Restarts are anticipated long before the headline. Don't open new buys in a stock for 5 sessions after its restart news; don't treat the headline as a reason to add.

facts.topic: Other news types (archive 2019-2026)
facts.answer: Contract, disruption, geopolitics, jobs, opposition, politics and production headlines show no consistent effect on the named stock over 5 or 20 days. Regulation news for power names leaned positive (+2.0% / +2.3% over 20 days in 2019-22 / 2023-26) but not strongly enough to trade. There is no free daily uranium futures history (UX=F on Yahoo has only today's price).

facts.topic: After-hours moves overshoot (minute data 2016-2026, our stocks)
facts.answer: When one of our stocks drops 3%+ after hours on a normal night, the next morning recovers about half of it (live rule 'ah_dip': +1.9% a trade 2016-23, about +0.8% in 2024-26 after the limit buffer and costs, n 42; still positive but smaller). On EARNINGS nights the after-hours move is real news and does not reverse; the rule skips them. After-hours JUMPS used to fade by the morning, but not since 2024 (+0.1% from selling into them), so the after-hours bank rule is off. Heavy buying in the last 30 minutes fades slightly the next day.

facts.topic: Your notebook ideas on Patient Levels fills (vol_pct>4, open_fill, Wednesday, group_up False, ret5d>10, AI power better, BWXT worse)
facts.answer: Checked 2026-11-25 on all 9,844 practice-book trades (Jan 2024 to Nov 2026), split at Aug 2025, and separately on nuclear vs other names. Average trade +0.23R. HOLDS in both halves and both name sets: (1) fills at the 9:30 open (gap into the level) earn about 0.13-0.15R less (t -2.4 / -2.1), still positive (+0.23 / +0.09R); (2) fills when the stock's group is below its 10-day average earn less (+0.13 vs +0.48R older, t -5.8; +0.12 vs +0.21R newer, t -1.5); (3) stocks 8%+ under their 10-day average at the fill earn less (-0.21 vs +0.36R older, +0.02 vs +0.17R newer). Weak or NO: hourly swings >4% of price (worse but n small, t -1), ran 10%+ in 5 days (t -1.6 / -0.4), Wednesday (better older, flat newer: no), AI power better (t +0.7 / +0.4: no real edge), BWXT worse (both halves but t about -1, n 165: weak). From minute data on our 11 nuclear stocks: heavy selling in the prior day's last 30 minutes is worse in both halves (t -0.7 / -2.1); pre-market volume 3x normal does nothing. How to use: none of these turn a trade negative, so they are reasons to size a fill smaller or wait for a second look, not to skip it. Only ~3 years of hourly data exist, one market era, so no written rule yet; keep scoring them live.

facts.topic: Chasing breakouts out of quiet, tight ranges (squeezes, narrow-range days, inside days)
facts.answer: Tested 2026-11-25 on 88 nuclear/related stocks and, independently, 140 big stocks, buying the next close vs the S&P after 0.2% costs, 2008-18 and 2019-26. Buying the break above a narrow-range (NR7) day loses about 0.2% in 5 days in all four tests (t -2.3 to -5.3, ~37,000 trades), also in uptrends. Breaking out of the tightest 20-day Bollinger squeeze of the past 6 months: -0.5% / -0.4% (ours), -0.1% / -0.5% (big stocks) over 10 days. Breakdowns from squeezes and inside days: nothing either way. A calm uptrend (own volatility in its lowest 20%) flips sign between eras. Lesson for levels: a quiet stock popping through its range is not a buy signal; our edge is buying at support, not chasing the first move out of a range.

facts.topic: How to read the team's own predictions so far (calls list, Nov 23-25)
facts.answer: Of the first 72 agent predictions, 61 say 'down' and 11 'up', made in a week the basket fell, so many down calls look right only because everything fell; the up calls are mostly wrong so far. None has reached its scoring date yet (track records are empty). So several agents agreeing on 'down' is not yet evidence: it is one market move counted many times. Make a call only when you would bet on it, say 'no view' otherwise, and wait for the scored record before trusting anyone's calls.

facts.topic: What PJM capacity-auction results do to the power stocks (VST, NRG, CEG, TLN, PEG, EXC), for the Dec 15 2029/30 auction
facts.answer: The last 10 auction results (2015-2025), stocks vs the utilities ETF (XLU). When the price went UP (5 auctions): +1.8% in the 2 days of the release, then -3.0% over the next 20 sessions (4 of 5 negative: the pop gets sold). When it went DOWN (5): flat reaction, ~0 after. The last one (Dec 17 2025, at the cap again, +1%) gave -1.7% on the day and -5.5% over 20 sessions. The 2029/30 auction will very likely clear at or near the cap again, which is expected: do not buy the release-day pop, and a held power stock is better trimmed into it than added to. Only 5 up-auctions, so this is context for judgment, not a rule.

facts.topic: Uranium price vs the miners: divergences and the long-term contract price
facts.answer: Monthly Cameco/UxC data back to 1988 vs the miners (CCJ, UEC, DNN, UUUU, NXE) minus the S&P. When spot rises 5%+ but the miners lag, there is NO extra catch-up (next month +2.5% before 2019, n 17) compared with spot up and miners up (+3.3%): the live uranium_momentum rule already covers it. The long-term contract price used to lead (up month -> miners +3.0% next month before 2019, t 2.1; new 3-year high +3.4%) but not since 2019 (+0.6%, -0.1%): don't use it as a timing signal any more. Miners down 10%+ vs the S&P in a month while spot held up: +4.1% / +3.1% next month but t only ~1.

facts.topic: Warning signs that turned out NOT to matter for our basket: credit stress, the leader cracking first, gold, correlation, news floods
facts.answer: Tested 2026-11-25 on 2000-06, 2008-18 and 2019-26 (our 10 vs the S&P, 20 days). Junk-bond weakness (high-yield fund under its 100-day average, 2%+ off its high, or a 2% 10-day drop): our basket did about as well as or better than normal, so credit stress alone is not a reason to sell or skip buys. The basket's best stock over 60 days cracking 12%+ while the rest hold up: slightly worse for us, but the same pattern in chips, banks, energy and big tech does nothing: no signal. Gold up 5%+ in a month: mixed by era. Our stocks all moving together (high correlation) or all apart: flips by era. A flood of headlines on one stock in a day: -2.0% to -3.4% over the next 5 days but n small and it reverses by 20 days; the first headline after 30 quiet days: nothing reliable.

facts.topic: Price landmarks: all-time highs, round numbers ($50, $100...), fallen stocks turning, and Canadian holidays
facts.answer: Tested 2026-11-25 (88 nuclear/related + 140 big stocks, next close vs the S&P after costs, 2008-18 and 2019-26). New all-time high, or within 3% of it: about the same as any day (no 'too high to buy', no breakout bonus). First close above a round number ($5/$10/$50/$100 steps by price): -0.4% to -0.6% over 10 days in 2008-18, ~0 since: crossing a round number is not a reason to buy. A stock 70%+ below its all-time high closing back over its 50-day average: +1.0% to +2.4% over 20 days in all four tests, but -1.3% in 2000-06 and the stock lists are today's survivors (the ones that never came back are missing), so it is not trusted. Canadian market holidays (Victoria Day, Canada Day, Civic Holiday, Canadian Thanksgiving, Boxing Day) when New York is open: CCJ, NXE and DNN trade on ~60% of normal volume; a 3%+ move that day reversed by +2.9% the next day before 2019 (n 39) but only +0.7% since (n 29): don't chase a big move on a Toronto holiday.

facts.topic: Share issuance: companies diluting or buying back, and the Sprott uranium trust issuing units
facts.answer: Share-count history (Yahoo, 2017-2026, 84 of our and related stocks), next month vs the S&P: companies that diluted 20%+ in a year did -0.1% (2017-21) / +1.8% (2022-26); buybacks -0.2% / +1.2%; by quintile no pattern. Dilution trend alone is not a signal for us (single offerings are different: the drop after an offering is a known pattern). The Sprott Physical Uranium Trust can only issue new units (and buy uranium) at a premium. When it was issuing fast while the miners were already up 10%+ in a month, the miners did +6.3% more than the S&P over the next 20 sessions (n 12, 2021-26) vs +0.4% for a miner rally without issuance (n 37): issuance confirms a rally is backed by real buying. Small, one era: practice book only (sprott_issuing). Right now the trust trades ~17% BELOW its asset value and has not issued since August, so it is not buying uranium: one less buyer behind spot.

facts.topic: Calendar and ranking ideas checked: jobs-report Fridays, quarterly index expiration (quad witching), lottery/volatility/reversal rankings
facts.answer: Tested 2026-11-25 on 2000-07, 2008-18, 2019-26. Jobs-report Friday: our 10 vs the S&P +0.10% / -0.13% / +0.55%, no reliable edge; the Monday after is slightly better (+0.2-0.3%) but less than a round-trip cost. Quarterly expiration/rebalance Friday (third Friday of Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec): our 10 beat the S&P that day in all three periods (+0.73 / +0.45 / +0.31%) and lagged in the WEEK AFTER in all three (-0.35 / -0.11 / -0.65% vs a normal week of +0.58 / +0.05 / +0.54%); related stocks the same direction. Every t is under 1.6, so it is a mild tilt, not a rule: no reason to rush new discretionary buys into the week after Dec 18, 2026. Ranking our stocks each month by last month's biggest one-day gain ('lottery' stocks), odd volatility, last month's return or closeness to the 52-week high: no consistent winner or loser group; the textbook effects do not show up in our names.

facts.topic: How and when our rebound trades should sell (checked against the live rules)
facts.answer: Sharp-drop rebounds (down 15%+ in 5 sessions), 88 nuclear/related and 140 big stocks, 2008-18 and 2019-26, vs the S&P after costs: the LIVE exit (sell at a close that is +10% or more, else after 10 sessions) earned +1.55% / +1.51% per trade on ours. A resting limit order at +10% during the day did WORSE in all four tests (+1.03% / +1.08% ours; about 0.5% less), because stocks that touch +10% intraday usually close higher over the following days. +15% target: +1.43% / +1.40%; +6%: +0.92% / +1.47%; no target: +1.69% / +1.17%. Keep the live exit. Time of day (minute data, our 11 stocks 2016-2026): after a stock ran 10%+ over 5 sessions, the first 30 minutes are weak (-0.46% / -0.40% open to 10:00), so never sell a winner at the opening bell unless it is the gap bank; after a 10% drop, 10:00 to the close is positive (+0.41% / +0.29%), so buying near the close (as the rules do) beats buying in the morning.

facts.topic: When the panic rule and the sharp-drop rule want the same money, and whether to wait a day before buying a panic
facts.answer: 88 nuclear/related stocks, 2000-07 / 2008-18 / 2019-26, vs the S&P after costs. Stocks that qualify for BOTH rules on the same day are not reliably better than panic-only or sharp-drop-only picks (both: -0.79 / +0.42 / +2.13% over 6 days; panic only +0.49 / +0.68 / +1.45%; sharp only -0.65 / +0.67 / +1.32%): no reason to favor one rule when cash is short; spread the money. Waiting a day to 'confirm' a panic buy is worse: buying the next close only if that day was up earned -1.12 / +0.46 / +0.70% vs +0.09 / +0.60 / +1.65% buying on the panic day as the rule does. Buy on the day.

facts.topic: When one nuclear stock jumps on its earnings, what its peers do (sympathy moves)
facts.answer: 442 earnings of our 10 stocks, 2010-2026; peers = same group (miners CCJ/UEC/DNN/UUUU/NXE, power CEG/VST/TLN, fuel LEU/BWXT), vs the S&P after costs. When the reporter jumps 5%+, its peers jump with it the same day (+5.4% in 2010-18, +3.8% in 2019-26) and then GIVE IT BACK over the next 5 days (-3.4%, t -2.5; -1.0%, t -1.4); peers that lagged the reporter do no better (-3.6% / -1.5%). After a 5%+ earnings drop, peers slip a little more (-1.0% / -0.3%). Big non-nuclear stocks do NOT fade like this (+0.1% / +0.5%), so it is specific to our crowd-driven names. Use: never buy or add to a peer because a group mate beat earnings. But do NOT cut a live rebound trade (panic / sharp drop) on a sympathy jump: in 29 such trades, selling into the jump earned +0.58% / -1.01% vs +2.75% / -0.12% for the normal exit (2010-18 / 2019-26). Let the rule's exit work. The reporter itself is the earnings_pop rule's business. Weeks when 3+ miners report within 5 sessions: the miners lagged the S&P by about 2% that week in both periods (n 8 / 19): another reason not to buy miners into a crowded earnings week.

facts.topic: Patient Levels fills: the stock's own long trend matters (200-day average, distance from its 6-month low)
facts.answer: Checked 2026-11-25 on the 9,844 practice-book level trades (2024-2026), split by date AND by nuclear vs other names. A fill while the stock is BELOW its 200-day average earns much less in all four splits: +0.22 vs +0.35R (older), +0.02 vs +0.24R (newer), nuclear +0.05 vs +0.23R, others +0.14 vs +0.31R (t -1.9 to -3.4). A fill within 5% of the stock's 6-month weekly low also earns less (+0.03 to +0.10R vs +0.17 to +0.32R), and a fill 40%+ above that low earns more (t +1.9 to +4.6). Support levels work in uptrends, not as bottoms in downtrends. Use: in the current market a level buy under the 200-day deserves a smaller size; do not skip it on that alone. The S&P's own move during the day before the fill does NOT matter once measured without peeking (a first version that used the fill hour's own S&P bar showed a fake effect). Only one market era of hourly data, so this is sizing judgment, not yet a written rule. Whole-account check (practice trades on our 10 lineup names, 20% per trade, max 4 open, 0.1% cost): taking every level buy +28.7%/yr with a worst drop of -32.8%; skipping the ones below the 200-day +29.4%/yr with a worst drop of -19.8% (older half +24.0 vs +23.6%/yr, newer +32.5 vs +31.5%); half size below the 200-day +27.9%/yr, -25.7%. So on our names, passing on level buys under the 200-day kept the return and cut the worst drop by about a third. LONGER CHECK (round 36): a daily support-bounce stand-in (buy a close that tested and held the 20-day low, stop 2% under it, +1.5R target, 15 days) on 88 of our/related stocks and 140 big stocks, 2008-18 and 2019-26, shows the OPPOSITE or nothing: below the 200-day earned +0.07 / +0.10R vs +0.05 / +0.04R above (ours), +0.08 / +0.04R vs +0.09 / -0.02R (big stocks). So the 200-day effect is a 2024-26 pattern in the hourly engine, not a law: a sizing hint, not a reason to pass on a trade.

facts.topic: Rebound trades that aren't working by day 3, and sharp drops that land at a new 4-6 month low
facts.answer: Panic and sharp-drop trades, 88 nuclear/related stocks 2000-07 / 2008-18 / 2019-26 and 140 big stocks as a check, vs the S&P after costs. Selling a trade that is 5%+ under water at the day-3 close trims the worst losses a little (sharp drops: worst 5% -21.9 -> -17.9%, -20.6 -> -12.8%, -20.6 -> -15.2%) but gives up return (panic +0.49 -> +0.22%, +1.61 -> +1.09%; big-stock sharp drops 2008-18 +1.46 -> +0.59%): no early 'not working' exit; let the rule run its days. Sharp drops that close within 3% of their 120-day low (a breakdown to new lows) earned less in our names in all three periods (-1.33 vs +1.45%, +0.55 vs +1.13%, +0.61 vs +1.67%) but not in big stocks (+1.64 vs +1.34% in 2008-18): a reason for the PM to lean to the small size on a sharp drop that is also a fresh multi-month low, not a skip.

facts.topic: Sharp-drop rebounds in the speculative reactor/fuel names (OKLO, SMR, NNE, LTBR, ASPI, URG, LEU)
facts.answer: 2019-2026, live sharp-drop exit, vs the S&P after costs. They rebound about as well on average as everything else (2023-26: +2.59% vs +2.77% a trade; median even higher, +8.4% vs +3.9%), but the worst 5% of trades are about twice as bad (-21.1% vs -12.5%). Same edge, double the tail: in these names take the base size only, never the deep-drop upsizing or the second add, and never two of them at once.

facts.topic: Can we catch a news move early (fast lane)?
facts.answer: No. Minute data 2016-2026 on our 11 stocks: power deals gap up ~10% at the open and buying at 9:35-9:45 earned about 0% to the close and -4% to -5% over 20 days; 2026 NRC approvals faded within days. Stocks already up 5%+ by 9:45 on 3x normal opening volume earned +0.3% for the rest of the day and +0.6% / +1.8% over 5 days after costs (worst 5%: -10% / -16%); their 20-day gain matched the hot stretch they were already in. The move is priced by the open: never size up on a headline; at most the normal rules apply.

facts.topic: Panic / sharp-drop trades that would hold through the stock's own earnings report
facts.answer: Our 10 stocks, 442 earnings dates 2010-2026, live exits, vs the S&P after costs. When the stock reported earnings inside the hold, the trade averaged -1.68% (2010-18, n 17) and +0.95% (2019-26, n 26), vs +2.95% and +1.80% with no earnings in the window. Small samples but the same direction both times: when a rebound buy would sit through earnings, lean to the small size (each stock's next earnings date is in your catalysts list; the Patient Levels trades already exit before earnings). When the drop itself WAS the earnings reaction, results flip by era (-5.3%, n 9 / +2.8%, n 40): no rule.

facts.topic: AI scare days (NVIDIA -6%+): is buying the power names a real pattern or AI-era luck?
facts.answer: Checked 2026-11-25 against past hype booms with the same setup (leader crashes, buy its picks-and-shovels names at the close, 10 sessions, vs the S&P after costs, compared with any day in that boom). AI 2024-26 (NVIDIA -6% -> CEG/VST/TLN): +8.6% vs a normal +1.3%, up 9 of 11 times (edge +7.4%, t 3.3). Dot-com 1998-2002 (Cisco -6% -> network/chip suppliers): edge +0.2% (36 scares). EVs 2019-23 (Tesla -6% -> lithium/battery/charging): -0.5% (34). Crypto 2017-22 (bitcoin -10% -> miners): -3.5% (11). So the pattern is NOT a general law of hype cycles; it has only worked for the AI-power names, possibly because power has real contracted demand while the others were pure sentiment, or because 11 events can be luck. Treat an AI scare day as a good, not guaranteed, setup for the power names: normal size, never oversized. It stays in the practice book (ai_scare) and today (Nov 25, NVIDIA about -8%) is a live test.

facts.topic: Nov 25 2026 morning drop and recovery: did the desk buy the dip on purpose? Should we keep more cash for days like this?
facts.answer: No deliberate dip buy happened. The S&P opened about -2.2% and recovered to about flat; the account went from about $935 at 9:45 to about $1,008 by 2 pm only because lots bought earlier (panic lots Nov 20, Thanksgiving and sharp-drop lots Nov 24) bounced with the market. The only order today was selling parked SPY at 9:38 to repay a $353 overspend, near the low. The level agent skipped every support buy because the basket was below its 10-day average. The panic rule could not have fired anyway: it judges the day at 3:30 pm and the S&P was no longer down 2%. Tested 2026-11-25: (1) Keeping 10-30% cash reserved for panic buys over the whole stack 2008-26 did not help (0% reserve 23.2%/yr, 10% 23.2%, 20% 22.7%, 30% 22.4%; worst drop -41 to -42% in all), because idle cash is already parked and sold on demand and the panic rule is capped at 3 names. (2) Buying stocks that open down 3%+ at the open when the S&P opens down 2%+, holding 5 days: +5.6% a trade and +2.2% vs the S&P in 2008-18, but -1.5% and -0.35% vs the S&P in 2019-26 (25 days), driven by March 2020 when it lost 15-27% in 5 days. Without Feb-Apr 2020 it was +4% in both eras, but crashes can't be left out in real life. So don't buy morning gap-downs as a rule and don't raise the cash floor; a one-day bounce is not evidence the desk learned anything.

facts.topic: Does the market drop most Thanksgivings, and can we catch holiday dips? (owner's idea, tested 2026-11-25)
facts.answer: The premise is false: in Thanksgiving week the S&P dipped 1%+ below the prior Friday in only 32% of years (ordinary weeks 52%) and the week finished up 74% of years (ordinary 57%); our 10 dipped 3%+ in 53% of stock-years vs 61% normally. Thanksgiving week is calmer and stronger than usual, not a reliable drop. Seven variants tested (about 20 counting thresholds), entries only by resting limit orders set from yesterday's close, so no look-ahead. FAILED: buying stocks that open down 2%+ on the Wednesday (2019-25 -0.8%), adding to the Thanksgiving trade when it falls 3% (2019-25 -0.45%), the Monday after Thanksgiving (worse than an ordinary Monday), and holding pre-holiday dips 2 extra sessions (edge gone in 2019-25). SURVIVED, small: (1) tg_week_dip, a limit 5% under yesterday's close Mon-Wed of Thanksgiving week on our 10, sold at the Black Friday close: +7.9%/buy in 2007-18 and +4.5% in 2019-25 vs -0.4%/+0.8% for the same trade in ordinary weeks, and ~600 other stocks agree (+3.5%/+1.9%), but only 14 weeks had fills in our 10 (t 1.5-2.5) and the big years were 2008 and 2020. (2) holiday_dip, a limit 3% under yesterday's close in the 3 sessions before any market holiday on our 10 plus related stocks, sold at the first close after: +0.32%/+0.52% a buy vs -0.05%/+0.12% on ordinary days (t 2.1/2.4), but ~600 other stocks show nothing, only 53% of holidays made money, and July 4, Labor Day and Presidents Day lost. Both went into the practice book (recent.py), no money, scored one average per day because same-day fills are one bet. Today's (Nov 25) fills are the day that gave us the idea, so don't count them as proof. Revisit after 30+ scored days.

facts.topic: Selling a trade that is doing well to fund a better new signal (owner's idea, tested 2026-11-25)
facts.answer: Whole stack 2008-26, 10% cash floor, costs included; baseline 23.2%/yr (2008-18 17.3%, 2019-26 32.0%), worst drop -40.7%. Swapping when CASH is short almost never happens (6-21 times in 18 years) because idle money is parked and sold on demand, and every version was flat or worse. The real limit is the 3-trade cap per rule. Swapping when the SLOTS are full: (a) panic slots, any version, WORSE (selling stuck panic lots to buy new ones: 21.1%/yr, worst drop -48%); (b) sharp-drop slots, selling the open sharp-drop lot with the biggest gain to buy a fresh 15%+ drop: gain 0%+ worse (22.7%), +3% mixed (16.8/33.7), +5% 17.8/32.7, +6% 17.8/33.3 (24.1%/yr, $59k vs $52k, 27 swaps), +7% 18.0/32.4, +8% 17.6/31.9 (12 swaps), +10% never triggers (the +10% take-profit sells first). Over the next 5 days the new trade beat the sold one by +2.3% (2008-18, n 11) and +1.8% (2019-26, n 16) at +6%, and +4.0/+2.8% at +7%, but -1.1% in 2019-26 at +5%. Selling a stuck loser instead is worse. Read: a sharp-drop rebound that is already up 6-7% has used most of its expected bounce (target +10%), while a fresh 15% drop has all of it ahead. Passes both eras narrowly at 6-7%, roughly 1-2 swaps a year, about +0.5-0.9%/yr; small sample. Candidate for the paper bot: swap a sharp-drop lot up 6%+ for a new sharp-drop signal when all 3 sharp slots are full; never swap panic lots.

facts.topic: Do people sell before holidays and buy back after? (owner's father's idea, tested 2026-11-25)
facts.answer: No, it's the opposite. S&P 500 1950-2026, 699 holidays: the last 3 sessions before a holiday averaged +0.34% (1950-89), +0.27% (1990-2007), +0.41% (2008-26) vs +0.07% for ordinary 3-day stretches; the last day before was up 70% / 51% / 63% of the time. The first day after is ordinary (+0.08 / +0.06 / -0.03%). Selling 3 days before and rebuying after would have missed about +0.3-0.4% per holiday and lost in 59-62% of holidays. Our 10 nuclear stocks are even stronger before holidays: last 3 days +0.82% (2008-18) and +1.50% (2019-26) vs +0.06% ordinary, last day before +0.26% / +0.67%. This is the well-known pre-holiday effect. Untested as a trading rule yet (buy 3 days before, sell at the last close before).
